newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian Starch and Glucose profits up.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian Starch and Glucose profits up.

text.p: Egyptian Starch and Glucose said on Friday it made net after-tax profits of 24.444 million pounds ($7.2 million) in the financial year 1995/6, 8.3 percent up on 22.566 million in the previous year.
The profits are equivalent to 5.31 pounds for each of the 4.6 million shares, which closed the week on the Egyptian stock exchange at 40.00 pounds a share.

The company did not mention a dividend for the year but it set aside 18.400 million pounds, exactly 4.00 pounds a share, for distribution to shareholders after deducting allocations to reserves, workers, board members and so on. The equivalent in the previous year was 18.252 million.
The company went majority private-sector in June when the state sold off more than 2.75 million of the shares at a fixed price of 35 pounds as part of its privatisation programme.
The company said sales in 1995/6 were worth 156.957 million pounds, 25.1 percent up on 125.429 million in 1994/5.
Profits before tax were 31.410 million, up from 27.000 million, it added.
It said that at the end of the year shareholders' rights were worth 54.951 million pounds, compared with 51.445 million one year earlier.
The state's Food Industries Company retains a 40.1 percent stake in Egyptian Starch and Glucose.
